note: Phase 1 covers only contracts with no external Circle/Pyth/ERC-8004 mainnet dependency. Confirmed by direct on-chain probe 2026-07-30: the native USDC ERC-20 view precompile at 0x3600...0000 IS live on mainnet at the same fixed address as testnet, but the testnet EURC token, Pyth oracle, and ERC-8004 Identity/Reputation/Validation Registry addresses all return no code on mainnet — nobody has deployed/published those there yet. Every contract below needed no address but our own and USDC. 2026-07-31: rpc.blockdaemon.mainnet.arc.io (used for the phase-1 deploy above) started returning 401 with no warning and stayed down — no official Circle RPC/explorer for Arc Mainnet is public yet. arc-rpc.stakeme.pro / arc.exploreme.pro is third-party, unofficial infrastructure, independently verified (chainId, real transaction/balance/bytecode cross-checks against our own known state) but not Circle's own; swap it out the moment an official endpoint exists.

feeRoutingFix2026_09_05.note: A full fee-routing sweep (does every fee-charging contract's treasury actually reach 0xF1CBe360...05CaF?) found ArcPay mainnet's immutable treasury still set to the deployer EOA (0x7D9b5ab1...40C2) — the same bug class as the 2026-08-02 fix below, just not caught in that sweep since ArcPay wasn't audited then. Only 0.00003 USDC had accrued (no real invoice volume yet). Redeployed to 0x69af28c7...3A9A2 with treasury correctly set to the multisig, verified live via treasury()/FEE_BPS() reads against the new contract, not the deploy script's log. arcPay above now points at the fixed contract; the old one is arcPayLegacyWrongTreasury. Everything else checked in the same sweep was already correct: marketUsdcFactoryV10, marketPairFactory, externalV3FeeRouter, and all 5 ArcBridgeRouter deployments (Arc/Ethereum/Optimism/Arbitrum/Base) all read back the real treasury. Known, unfixed, zero-impact: agentPayFactory and agentPayFactoryV6 both have an immutable internal reference to the OLD ArcPay (set at their own construction, can't be repointed without redeploying those factories too) — but both report vaultCount() 0 on Arc Mainnet, so no real Agent Pay invoice has ever settled through either path.

graduationPoolGriefingFix2026_08_30.note: marketUsdcFactoryV10 redeployed: 0xCEc317Ca...19cED (now marketUsdcFactoryV10LegacyPoolGriefing) pre-created each launch's Uniswap V3 pool at launch time, left uninitialized — anyone could call initialize() with an arbitrary starting price before graduation, and the graduation mint used amount0Min/amount1Min of 0, so a front-run price was accepted silently and most of the LP reserve could be stranded permanently. Fixed factory (0xCf93231d...b6feD3) creates and initializes the pool atomically inside _graduate() instead, with a real slippage floor on the mint and a revert if a pool is somehow already mispriced. Same v3Factory/positionManager/treasury/graduationThreshold (12,000 ether) as before — only the graduation mechanics changed. The old factory's existing launches (including "Architects") are not migratable and stay indexed/tradeable there; every new launch now goes through the fixed factory. See contracts/test/ArcPumpV10Graduation.t.sol for the regression tests.

feeRoutingFix2026_08_02.note: Auditing 'does swap fee reach treasury' surfaced two contracts whose immutable `treasury` was set to the deployer EOA (0x7D9b5ab1...40C2) instead of the real treasury (0xF1CBe360...05CaF): marketPairFactory (0 pairs ever created there — clean swap, nothing to migrate) and marketUsdcFactoryV9 (the live 1% bonding-curve fee path — ~0.04 USDC had accrued, withdrawable only by the deployer EOA, and every future launch would have inherited the same bug since treasury is set once per factory and inherited by every curve it spawns). Both replaced with freshly deployed, correctly-configured factories, verified with treasury() reads against both before cutover. The old V9 factory's one live launch ("Architects") is not migratable (treasury is immutable per already-deployed curve) and stays indexed as a legacy factory; the old pair factory is simply abandoned (never used). Uninvolved and unaffected: externalV3FeeRouter (0.30% external-pool swap fee) already correctly pointed at the real treasury. Also worth knowing: post-graduation trading fees on Arcodian's OWN V9 pools are NOT collected by treasury at all — the LP position is minted straight to a burn address at graduation (by design, so liquidity can never be pulled/rugged), so that 0.30% accrues to the burned LP forever, not to anyone. The only per-swap fee treasury actually earns today is the external-V3-venue 0.30% and the pre-graduation 1% curve fee.

bridge.note: ArcBridgeRouter (1.5% fee on top of Circle's canonical CCTP v2 TokenMessengerV2/MessageTransmitterV2, same deterministic addresses across every chain listed here). Deployed once arc-rpc.stakeme.pro proved Arc Mainnet was actually reachable; a prior deployment had a Solidity interface bug (declared a uint64 nonce return that CCTP v2's real depositForBurn doesn't have) that reverted every single bridge call on every chain since its original deployment — fixed, redeployed, and proven with real transactions on all 5 chains, including a full Arc-to-Base-to-Arc-equivalent round trip and independent third-party wallets bridging on their own. Circle's own TokenMinter.burnLimitsPerMessage caps a single burn OUT of Arc — a network-side rollout limit, not ours, that Circle raises over time: 1 USDC when first confirmed 2026-07-31, already 100,000 USDC by 2026-08-30. The frontend reads this limit live instead of hardcoding it (fetchBurnLimitPerMessage in src/bridgeRecovery.ts).
bridge.inboundAttestationStuck: Confirmed 2026-08-30: outbound burns FROM Arc get a real Circle attestation (status "complete") within minutes — e.g. 0xac40c8ee...79e8a5 (Arc→Arbitrum) and 0x790ac8f2...48c9227 (Arc→Base), both source domain 26, both complete. But real burns INTO Arc from another chain never get attested: three Arbitrum→Arc burns (0xdccd1211...5f8d0b0, 0xfc3ac4fb...39eec, 0x772e8f02...d4c2ada, destination domain 26) sit at attestation "PENDING" / status "pending_confirmations" indefinitely, including ones from blocks tens of millions old on Arbitrum — no amount of waiting completes them. The on-chain contracts are fine on both sides (Arc's TokenMinter.getLocalToken(3, arbUSDC) correctly resolves to Arc's native USDC, so the token link exists); this is Circle's off-chain attestation SERVICE not yet attesting messages where Arc is the destination domain, consistent with Arc Mainnet still being pre-public-launch (Circle's own Sept 16, 2026 date). Nothing in Arcodian's bridge code can fix this — it will presumably start working once Circle turns on inbound attestation for Arc's domain. Re-check this note after Sept 16, 2026.

governance.note: 2026-08-02: ArcAdminTimelock's admin (the role that can change who may propose/execute, or transfer admin again) was migrated from the deployer EOA to a freshly-deployed 2-of-3 ArcMultisig (contracts/src/ArcGovernance.sol) via transferAdmin/acceptAdmin — verified on-chain, admin() now returns the multisig. isProposer/isExecutor were left as the deployer alone (routine timelock operations stay single-key; only the higher-privilege admin role required 2 signatures to change). ArcMultisig itself has NO owner-rotation function — its signer set is immutable once deployed, so this is a one-shot decision. All 3 signer keys were generated on and are stored on the same VPS that runs this project (not independent devices/parties) — this multisig protects against a single lost/misused key, not against compromise of this server itself. See docs/ARCODIAN-AUDIT-READINESS.md; ArcAdminTimelock's own contract docstring still says 'Not audited, not for mainnet' — this migration does not change that.
